events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
Case type is route_deviation and the trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so distance drives the fare: actual 12.4 km against a 10.8 km optimal route, +1.6 km [F1][F6][RD-2]. The rider asked only for the extra distance back, and both sides now converge on a $1.09 figure, but I cannot rule on the merits because the chat contains a threat-keyword hit.

The chat record shows the rider's message #1 at 09:35 ("I'll find you at the lobby, I am in a red jacket.") carrying a detected threat keyword ("find you") [F7][F8]. Where chat materials contain threat or intimidation language, no automatic ruling is issued and the case is escalated with a factual summary [F8][SAFE-1]. This is a threshold bar on adjudication, independent of the route question, so no refund is computed here.

For the human reviewer, the factual position on the route dispute: there is exactly one recorded off-route segment, 09:49–09:52, where 2.15 km was driven over a 1.38 km optimal stretch, adding 0.77 km and straying up to 1019 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. No consent exemption is available — the chat shows only the rider's 09:35 lobby message and the driver's post-hoc statement "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me", with no pre-departure route proposal or agreement timestamped before the segment's 09:49 start [F7][F9][RD-5]. No traffic exemption is available either: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F12], and the only speed records, the Ayer Rajah and Central Expressway entries at band 4 (30–39 km/h) [F10][F11], are above the band 1–2 threshold in RD-4(b) and are not tied to the substituted optimal stretch; weather was fair [F13], so RD-4(a) and (b) both fail [RD-4]. Segment F3 is therefore an unexempted off-route segment under RD-1.

If the reviewer clears the chat, the money follows RD-2 for a RydeTAXI trip: per-km rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $17.47 ÷ 12.4 km = $1.41/km [F6][RD-2]; refund = 0.77 km × $1.41/km = $1.09. The billed excess of 1.6 km / $2.30 [F1][F4] is not the measure: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, and the remaining 0.83 km is map-matching residue that is not refunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. Waiting was $0.00 [F6], so no RD-3(c) stop adjustment arises; the 18.9 min vs 17 min duration difference [F2] is not tied to any adjustable meter component.

claims.assertion: This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres driven directly increase the fare; the GPS record shows 12.4 km driven against a 10.8 km optimal route, i.e. +1.6 km (+15%).
One unexempted off-route segment exists: 09:49–09:52, where 2.15 km was driven over an optimal-route stretch of 1.38 km, adding 0.77 km and straying up to 1019 m from the optimal route.

The driver never asked the rider before leaving the optimal route: the chat contains no route-change proposal and no rider agreement, only the driver's post-hoc statement 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me.'

No exemption applies under RD-4: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route in the trip window, and the only speed records (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY, speed band 4, 30–39 km/h) are not band 1 or 2 severe congestion and are not tied to the substituted optimal-route stretch.
Fare exposure at the metered rate: the billed excess of 1.6 km × $1.41/km = $2.30, and the segment's unexempted 0.77 km is $1.09 at that same per-km rate ($17.47 ÷ 12.4 km).

The deviation is chargeable to the rider only through the meter, and refund is limited to the unexempted segment's extra distance; the residual gap between the billed 1.6 km and the 0.77 km segment is map-matching residual and is not claimed.

A flag_account request is warranted because the driver's 90-day record shows 4 disputes with 2 upheld alongside 889 trips, indicating a pattern the platform should review; this fact is offered only to support the ancillary account action.

weaknesses: The driver's account is long-standing (1620 d, 4.8 rating) with 2 upheld disputes but 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days (F15), so the RD-6 'repeated' predicate is not met and the flag_account request may be refused.

The GPS record shows the off-route segment added only 0.77 km while the rider was billed for 1.6 km excess (F1 vs F3); the 0.83 km difference is not attributable to any identified unexempted segment under RD-2, so the judge may cap any refund at the segment figure rather than the full $2.30.

The chat's threat-keyword tag on the rider's 09:35 'I'll find you at the lobby' message (F7, F8) is a benign meet-up line in context, but the other side may use it to portray the rider's account; it is not addressed by any RD clause and I do not rely on it.

Speed band 4 congestion records (F10, F11) do exist on expressways in the trip window, and the driver may argue they explain the reroute; they fail RD-4 only because they are band 4 and not matched to the substituted stretch.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment is 09:49-09:52, adding 0.77 km (2.15 km driven vs 1.38 km optimal), so the rider's claim of a 12 km detour rests on a single 0.77 km segment, not on a wholesale different route.

The driver did not reroute without cause: the diversion happened inside a window when both the Ayer Rajah Expressway and the Central Expressway were recorded at speed band 4 (30-39 km/h), i.e. degraded conditions on the corridor, while no incidents were recorded elsewhere (F12) and weather was fair (F13).

No traffic-incident fact supports the segment as a justified reroute (F12 records no incidents near the route), and band 4 is far above the band 1-2 congestion threshold, so excuse (a) under RD-4 cannot be established for the 0.77 km segment.

No chat or app record shows the rider named or approved the diverted route before the segment began; the only rider message is about a meeting point and the driver's statement about GPS rerouting is not backed by any pre-departure agreement.

This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the metered distance is billed at $1.41/km; the correctly computed overcharge for the unexempted 0.77 km segment is 0.77 x $1.41 = $1.09, which is the maximum the rider can recover on the distance item.

The rider's claimed figure of a full 1.2-1.6 km refund is overstated: the fare fact shows excess distance billed of $2.30 for the full 1.6 km of extra driving, of which only the 0.77 km attributable to the off-route segment is refundable under RD-2, the remainder being map-matching residue that is not refunded.

The remaining distance ($17.47 for 12.4 km), time component ($4.92) and platform fee ($1.47) are published meter-based charges not disputed by RD-2, and no unexempted segment beyond the 0.77 km is recorded, so they stand.

No halt waiting charge was levied (waiting $0.00), so there is nothing to adjust for a stop under RD-3(c), and the trip's 18.9 min versus 17 min estimate is a 1.6 min difference not tied to any disputed charge.
The driver has 889 trips in 90 days and 4 disputes with 0 route deviations upheld, so this case does not make him a repeat route offender and no account flag is warranted on these facts.

weaknesses: The strongest adverse fact is F3: a 0.77 km off-route segment starting at 09:49 with no prior passenger agreement (F7 shows only a lobby message, F9 is the driver's own uncorroborated claim), which is an unexempted deviation under RD-1 and triggers a partial refund under RD-2.

The driver's reroute justification fails on the evidence: F10 and F11 show only band 4 (30-39 km/h) congestion while RD-4(b) requires band 1 or 2, and F12 confirms no traffic incident at all, so the rider/other side will argue the deviation was purely discretionary and RD-4(a) is unavailable.

points.response: Concede: the refundable amount does not depend on the rider's colloquial '12 km' phrasing but on the recorded segment; F3 identifies one unexempted segment of 0.77 km, which is exactly what my claim C5/C6 quantifies.

Band 4 (30-39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah and Central Expressways is not the band 1-2 severe congestion RD-4 recognises, and F10/F11 are not tied to the substituted 1.38 km stretch of the optimal route, so no reasonable cause is shown; the driver's own concession in D3 confirms this.

This is the driver's own point and it is adverse to him: with no traffic-incident fact (F12) and no band 1-2 record, RD-4(a) and (b) both fail and the 09:49-09:52 segment stands as unexempted under RD-1.

Agreed and it is the core of the rider's case: F7 contains only a lobby meet-up message, and the driver's F9 'GPS rerouted me' statement is made after the fact, so nothing preceded the segment as RD-5 requires for consent.
Concede the arithmetic: 0.77 km (F3) x the $1.41/km rate derivable from F6 ($17.47 ÷ 12.4 km) = $1.09, which is the amount the rider asks for.
Concede that the full 1.6 km billed excess (F1, F4) is not claimed; the rider's request is limited to the 0.77 km segment under RD-2, and the rider's brief already excluded the map-matching residue.

Not contested as to the published meter components, but the $1.09 of distance inside the unexempted segment is not a legitimate meter component for the driver to keep under RD-2, and that is the only sum sought.
Correct that waiting is $0.00 (F6) and no RD-3(c) stop adjustment arises; the rider makes no stop or waiting claim, and F2's 1.6 min excess is cited only as context for the longer route (F1).

Concede that the RD-6 predicate is not met: neither F14 nor F15 shows a route deviation upheld in the last 90 days, so the rider withdraws the flag_account request in C7; the driver's 2 upheld disputes out of 4 (F15) do not by themselves satisfy RD-6.

Accepted that this is a metered RydeTAXI trip where distance drives the fare (F1, F6), but RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km at the per-km rate, not the whole +1.6 km gap between actual and optimal.
The off-route segment record is not contested: F3 shows 0.77 km added at 09:49-09:52, and that is the single segment against which RD-2 is computed for my client.

Agreed that the chat contains only the rider's 09:35 lobby message (F7) and my client's post-hoc statement (F9), so no pre-departure agreement satisfies RD-5 and the segment is not exempted on consent grounds.

I concede the RD-4 exemption fails on the traffic record: F12 shows no incidents near the route and F10/F11 record only band 4 (30-39 km/h), while RD-4(b) requires band 1-2, so the deviation stands as unexempted.
The per-km arithmetic is correct: $17.47 ÷ 12.4 km = $1.41/km, so 0.77 km × $1.41 = $1.09, which is exactly the refund my client already concedes (F3, F4, F6).

Agreed, and this converges with my claim D6: the $2.30 billed excess (F4) is not the measure of refund, the refund is capped at the unexempted segment, and no party claims the 0.83 km residual (F1, F3).

The flag_account request must be refused: RD-6 requires a route dispute upheld in the last 90 days, and F15 records 0 route disputes upheld for my client (2 upheld disputes are not route-based), so the 'repeated' predicate is absent; additionally his 4.4-year account, 4.8 rating and 889 trips in 90 days (F15) show no abuse pattern, and profile facts cannot decide the case (see also F14, no route disputes upheld for the rider either).

I withdraw the framing in D1 to the extent it read as contesting the existence of the segment: the segment is real per F3, and my brief's operative position is already the $1.09 partial refund, not a no_action.
